<!-- ORIGIN COMMENT — please read before adding anything below.

     Automated agents working this repository end their pull-request body with
     a single HTML comment naming the agent brand that authored the change. The
     canonical review coordinator reads that comment to route the review to the
     *other* brand, so three rules govern it, and parsers enforce all three:

     1. It must be the body's LAST non-whitespace content. Anything placed
        after it — a signature, a checklist, one more note — stops it counting
        as the marker, and routing fails.

     2. It must occur exactly once. The parsers match the token anywhere in the
        body, so writing it out a second time, in prose or inside a comment
        such as this one, reads as a duplicate and routing fails just the same.
        That is why this comment describes the marker rather than showing it,
        and why you should not paste it in from another pull request.

     3. There is no correct brand for a human-authored change, so it offers you
        no default: leave it out.

     If you are a human contributor, that means: change nothing in this comment,
     add nothing below it, and submit. A body carrying no origin marker is a
     supported state rather than a mistake — when the maintainer invokes the
     canonical review coordinator on it, an unmarked pull request is routed to
     both agent brands instead of one. -->
